## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Global Claude Code Architecture
2	
3	This document describes the architecture of this machine's global Claude Code setup. Read this before changing rules, hooks, or directory layout. Companion documents:
4	
5	- `HARNESS_ARCHITECTURE.md` — harness design pattern (3-Layer + Verification Loop, Anthropic-native), project-agnostic
6	- `CLAUDE.md` — operating rules (DO / DON'T)
7	- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
8	- `AUTOMATION.md` — session automation hooks (architecture diagram + auto-generated tables)
9	- `templates/order-match-checklist.md` — task self-verification template
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Operating Environment
14	
15	| Property | Value |
16	|---|---|
17	| OS | Windows 10 (native, no WSL) |
18	| Shell | Git Bash (primary) / PowerShell 5.1 |
19	| AI assistant | Claude Code (sole assistant — Codex / Cursor removed) |
20	| IDE host | VS Code with Claude Code extension |
21	| Drive layout | C drive (under `%USERPROFILE%`) for the `.claude` config root. Project work lives on D:; only the Claude infra itself is single-drive. |
22	
23	**Rationale (single-drive on C)**: cognitive simplicity, tool universality (every Windows tool assumes `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`), and vanilla compliance with Claude Code's default. C has 88+ GB free; the entire setup is ~165 MB.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 2. Directory Layout
28	
29	```
30	%USERPROFILE%\.claude\                     [single source of truth, plain dirs only — no junctions]
31	│
32	├── CLAUDE.md                              # operating rules (DO / DON'T)
33	├── RTK.md                                 # CLI proxy reference
34	├── AUTOMATION.md                          # session automation architecture + auto-marked tables
35	├── ARCHITECTURE.md                        # this file
36	│
37	├── settings.json                          # hook registrations + permissions + statusline
38	├── settings.local.json                    # per-host overrides (optional)
39	├── active-projects.json                   # pinned projects (cleanup.ps1 protection list)
40	├── .claude.json                           # Claude Code internal session state (autogenerated, do not edit)
41	├── .credentials.json                      # MCP auth (sensitive — never read / commit)
42	│
43	├── cleanup.ps1                            # SessionEnd cleanup + retention rotations
44	├── statusline.ps1                         # status line renderer (cwd | model | effort | sessions | warnings)
45	│
46	├── hooks/                                 # SessionStart / SessionEnd / Pre+PostCompact / PostToolUse hooks
47	├── templates/                             # project-init.md, order-match-checklist.md
48	├── plugins/                               # plugin metadata
49	├── ide/                                   # IDE settings
50	├── agents/                                # custom agent definitions (if any)
51	├── commands/                              # slash command definitions (if any)
52	│
53	├── projects/                              # per-project session state + memory
54	├── plans/                                 # active + archived plans
55	├── reports/                               # token-usage.md (append-only)
56	├── backups/                               # precompact-* snapshots + memory-YYYYWW.zip weekly
57	├── file-history/                          # UUID-keyed file version diffs
58	├── shell-snapshots/                       # shell context snapshots
59	├── sessions/                              # session state (ephemeral)
60	├── session-env/                           # SessionStart artifacts (memory-lint.txt, compact-warning.txt)
61	├── paste-cache/                           # clipboard cache (ephemeral)
62	├── downloads/                             # downloaded artifacts
63	├── telemetry/                             # telemetry queue
64	├── cache/                                 # generic cache
65	├── .docs-cache/                           # SHA256 hashes of upstream docs + prefix-version.txt
66	├── .drift-queue/                          # PostToolUse enqueue → drift-detect-worker drain
67	│
68	├── history.jsonl                          # session history log
69	└── cleanup.log                            # SessionEnd audit trail
70	
71	%USERPROFILE%\.claude-archive\             [out-of-band backups, separate from live config]
72	└── rollback-pre-consolidation.zip         # one-shot pre-D-removal snapshot
73	```
74	
75	**Anti-pattern**: do not create NTFS junctions to redirect any subdirectory to another volume. The previous D-split design was reverted because it complicated backup tooling, broke drive-letter assumptions in third-party scripts, and provided no measurable benefit at this data scale.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 3. Path Resolution Convention
80	
81	Every script and document references the config root via:
82	
83	```powershell
84	$ClaudeRoot = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) {
85	    $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
86	} else {
87	    Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude'
88	}
89	```
90	
91	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is **not set** in any registry scope — the env var fallback exists only to honor user overrides if a future need arises. The default code path always resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.
92	
93	In documentation: use `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows-native, expands in cmd / PowerShell / Git Bash) or `~/.claude/` for compactness.
94	
95	**Forbidden**: relocating the `.claude` config root to a non-profile drive (`D:\.claude\`, `D:\.claude-data\`). D-drive paths in project content are fine — the rule targets the infra root, not the project.
96	
97	---
98	
99	## 4. Hook Architecture
100	
101	Seven hook events are registered in `settings.json` (plus a `statusLine` renderer). SessionEnd registers two command entries, so total command count is eight. See `AUTOMATION.md` for the full sequence diagram and the auto-generated registration table.
102	
103	| Event | Purpose | Async |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| SessionStart | regenerate AUTO-marks, auto-pin, memory-lint, weekly memory-backup, 24h doc gate, 60d plan archive, **D-remnant detection → oneshot consolidation** | no |
106	| SessionEnd | retention rotations (13 categories), MEMORY.md link integrity, kill stale workers, drift queue drain | yes |
107	| PostToolUse (Edit\|Write\|Bash) | enqueue edited files / dep-install audits to `.drift-queue` | yes |
108	| UserPromptSubmit | inject git status + recent commits when repo is dirty (skip-when-clean keeps prompt cache warm) | no |
109	| PreCompact | hard-link snapshot of MUST-preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>` | no |
110	| PostCompact | verify `@import` chains + active plan readability; write `compact-warning.txt` on issues | yes |
111	| Stop | append rtk session stats to `reports/token-usage.md` | yes |
112	| statusLine | render status line (includes `compact:warn` indicator if PostCompact flagged a loss) | (poll) |
113	
114	**Design principle**: each hook runs in <100 ms in the synchronous path. Heavier work (`check-updates-worker`) is spawned detached via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`. Detached workers survive parent exit; PowerShell jobs do not.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Retention Policy
119	
120	Configured in `cleanup.ps1`. Pinned projects (via `active-projects.json`) are exempt from `projects/` rotation.
121	
122	| Directory | Retention | Notes |
123	|---|---|---|
124	| `plans/` | 2 days (file mtime) | drafts; archived plans go to `plans/archive/` after 60d |
125	| `shell-snapshots/` | 7 days | session shell context |
126	| `file-history/` | 14 days (dir mtime) | UUID-keyed |
127	| `projects/` | 30 days (dir mtime) | pinned + 14d grace exempt |
128	| `session-env/` | empty subdirs only | per-session SessionStart outputs |
129	| `backups/precompact-*` | 28 days | pre-compaction snapshots |
130	| `backups/memory-*.zip` | 56 days | weekly memory archive |
131	| `.docs-cache/` | 90 days (file mtime) | SHA hashes regenerable |
132	| `.drift-queue/` | 7 days | post-drain leftovers |
133	| `cache/` | 14 days | generic |
134	| `downloads/` | 30 days | |
135	| `paste-cache/` | 7 days | clipboard |
136	| `telemetry/` | 30 days | |
137	
138	Stale background workers >24h old are killed by command-line pattern match against `<ClaudeRoot>\hooks\`.
139	
140	---
141	
142	## 6. Compaction Policy (REWIND CONTEXT)
143	
144	When Claude Code reaches its context budget and triggers compaction:
145	
146	**MUST preserve** (load-bearing): active plan, all rule files (`CLAUDE.md` / `RTK.md` / `AUTOMATION.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md`), `settings.json`, per-project active `MEMORY.md`, memory topic files modified within last 30 days.
147	
148	**MAY drop** (regenerable): plans older than 60 days, `.docs-cache/*`, `cleanup.log`, completed prior-turn todos, intermediate exploration output.
149	
150	**Hooks**: `precompact-snapshot.ps1` hard-links the preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>/`. `postcompact-verify.ps1` validates `@import` chains and active-plan readability — writes `session-env/compact-warning.txt` on failure, which `statusline.ps1` surfaces as `compact:warn`.
151	
152	**Anti-pattern**: snapshotting `sessions/` or `file-history/` "just in case" — unbounded growth with no recovery use case (FOMO trap).
153	
154	---
155	
156	## 7. RTK Strategy (Token Optimization)
157	
158	RTK is a Rust-based CLI output filter (60–90% token savings). On this machine:
159	
160	- **Mode**: explicit prefix only (`rtk <command>`). Hook-based auto-rewrite is a WSL-only feature and is not used here.
161	- **Coverage**: noisy multi-line outputs (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files, `gh pr`, package managers).
162	- **Skip**: single-line outputs (`echo`, `pwd`).
163	
164	Detailed savings table: see `RTK.md`.
165	
166	---
167	
168	## 8. Order Match Verification
169	
170	Every non-trivial task ends with a self-verification step before the AI declares completion. Procedure (full template at `templates/order-match-checklist.md`):
171	
172	1. Restate the user's order verbatim.
173	2. List acceptance criteria (observable state).
174	3. Map each criterion to evidence (`file:line`, command output, test result).
175	4. Detect scope creep — anything done outside the order? Justify or revert.
176	5. Honor constraints — language (Korean chat / English AI artifacts), paths (no `D:\.claude`), tools, banned actions.
177	
178	If any criterion lacks evidence: do **not** declare done. Either complete the gap or report it explicitly.
179	
180	This rule is the system's primary safeguard against the "AI says done but didn't actually finish" failure mode.
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 9. Vanilla Compliance + FOMO Guard
185	
186	Two principles that govern every change to this setup:
187	
188	### Vanilla compliance
189	
190	The closer to stock Claude Code behavior, the easier upgrades and debugging become. Do **not** customize unless an incident or measurable cost forced it. Document the trigger when adding any non-default rule.
191	
192	Current non-vanilla customizations and their justifications:
193	
194	| Customization | Trigger |
195	|---|---|
196	| `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` | productivity in trusted host environment |
197	| 7 hook events (8 command entries — SessionEnd registers 2) in `settings.json` | upstream doc drift, plan rotation, prompt cache invalidation |
198	| `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` env | 1h prompt cache TTL for token efficiency |
199	| `effortLevel = "high"` | model output quality preference |
200	| 13-category retention in `cleanup.ps1` | unbounded growth in volatile dirs |
201	
202	### FOMO guard
203	
204	A feature looking interesting is not justification. Before adding a hook / script / rule / skill / plugin, point to:
205	
206	- a past incident the change prevents, OR
207	- a measurable benefit (token savings, time savings, error reduction)
208	
209	If neither exists: skip it.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## 10. AI Tool Exclusivity
214	
215	Claude Code is the sole AI assistant on this machine.
216	
217	- **Removed**: Codex CLI (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex`), Cursor (`%APPDATA%\Cursor`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-updater`).
218	- **Pending uninstall** (out of architecture scope, user-driven): VS Code extensions `openai.chatgpt-*`, `github.copilot-chat-*`, Cursor app binaries.
219	
220	Rationale: split AI surfaces produce conflicting context, duplicate token costs, and inconsistent rule application. One assistant = one rule set = predictable behavior.
221	
222	---
223	
224	## 11. Language Convention
225	
226	| Audience | Language |
227	|---|---|
228	| User-facing chat replies | Korean |
229	| AI-consumed artifacts (docs, hooks, plans, memory, comments, log lines) | **English** |
230	| Code identifiers, paths, commands, error messages | English (verbatim, regardless of context) |
231	| Quoted user phrases (e.g. "완료" / "done") | preserved as-is in either language |
232	
233	Rationale: AI consumption efficiency. English keeps tokens predictable across models and avoids encoding ambiguity (PowerShell 5.1 ANSI codepage corrupts em-dash and similar non-ASCII glyphs).
234	
235	---
236	
237	## 12. Migration History
238	
239	| Date | Change | Reason |
240	|---|---|---|
241	| 2026-04-28 | D-drive split (config on C, data on D via NTFS junctions) | initial separation experiment |
242	| 2026-04-28 | **Reverted to C-only single-drive** | cognitive complexity > benefit at 165 MB scale |
243	| 2026-04-28 | Codex / Cursor configs removed (12.1 GB reclaimed) | AI tool exclusivity |
244	| 2026-04-28 | `cleanup.ps1` extended (7 → 13 retention categories) | unbounded growth gap |
245	| 2026-04-28 | DO / DON'T format adopted in `CLAUDE.md` / `RTK.md` | rule clarity |
246	| 2026-04-28 | Order Match Verification introduced | "AI says done but didn't" failure mode |
247	| 2026-04-28 | Compaction policy formalized | REWIND CONTEXT optimization |
248	| 2026-04-28 | `permissions.deny` redesigned (8 → 24 portable patterns) | Old rules used `%USERPROFILE%` (cmd-only literal, doesn't expand in Bash) and hardcoded the username, so real destructive inputs (`~/.claude`, `/c/Users/...`, `C:/Users/...`) bypassed every rule. New set covers all shell forms and is account-agnostic. Colon-form `:*` aligned to space/inline form per official permission spec. Added `git clean`, `git checkout -- *`, `git restore .`, `**/.env*`. |
249	| 2026-04-28 | Project `.claude/settings.json` deny added (Drive policy enforcement) | Project AGENTS.md (per-project, not a global file) declared "D: drive only for project work" but no rule enforced it. Project-level deny overrides user-level (precedence: Project > User), so this is the layer that actually blocks `Write/Edit/rm -rf` on `C:\` from project context. Global infra edits now require `update-config` skill or an explicit `~/.claude` session. |
250	
251	---
252	
253	## 13. Maintenance Checklist
254	
255	Run periodically (weekly recommended):
256	
257	- [ ] `cleanup.log` — recent SessionEnd audit lines show all 13 retention counters firing.
258	- [ ] `docs-updates.md` — review any new entries from `check-updates-worker.ps1`.
259	- [ ] `review-needed.md` — drain drift findings.
260	- [ ] `reports/token-usage.md` — confirm rtk savings ratio is healthy (>50% on heavy days).
261	- [ ] `Get-PSDrive C` — free space stable; no runaway growth in `projects/` / `file-history/`.
262	- [ ] `Test-Path D:\.claude*` — must return `False` (single-drive guarantee).
263	- [ ] Architecture deltas not yet documented here? Append to section 12.

- `HARNESS_ARCHITECTURE.md` — harness design pattern (3-Layer + Verification Loop, Anthropic-native), project-agnostic
- `CLAUDE.md` — operating rules (DO / DON'T)
- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
- `AUTOMATION.md` — session automation hooks (architecture diagram + auto-generated tables)
- `templates/order-match-checklist.md` — task self-verification template

---

## 1. Operating Environment

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 10 (native, no WSL) |
| Shell | Git Bash (primary) / PowerShell 5.1 |
| AI assistant | Claude Code (sole assistant — Codex / Cursor removed) |
| IDE host | VS Code with Claude Code extension |
| Drive layout | C drive (under `%USERPROFILE%`) for the `.claude` config root. Project work lives on D:; only the Claude infra itself is single-drive. |

**Rationale (single-drive on C)**: cognitive simplicity, tool universality (every Windows tool assumes `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`), and vanilla compliance with Claude Code's default. C has 88+ GB free; the entire setup is ~165 MB.

---

## 2. Directory Layout

```
%USERPROFILE%\.claude\                     [single source of truth, plain dirs only — no junctions]
│
├── CLAUDE.md                              # operating rules (DO / DON'T)
├── RTK.md                                 # CLI proxy reference
├── AUTOMATION.md                          # session automation architecture + auto-marked tables
├── ARCHITECTURE.md                        # this file
│
├── settings.json                          # hook registrations + permissions + statusline
├── settings.local.json                    # per-host overrides (optional)
├── active-projects.json                   # pinned projects (cleanup.ps1 protection list)
├── .claude.json                           # Claude Code internal session state (autogenerated, do not edit)
├── .credentials.json                      # MCP auth (sensitive — never read / commit)
│
├── cleanup.ps1                            # SessionEnd cleanup + retention rotations
├── statusline.ps1                         # status line renderer (cwd | model | effort | sessions | warnings)
│
├── hooks/                                 # SessionStart / SessionEnd / Pre+PostCompact / PostToolUse hooks
├── templates/                             # project-init.md, order-match-checklist.md
├── plugins/                               # plugin metadata
├── ide/                                   # IDE settings
├── agents/                                # custom agent definitions (if any)
├── commands/                              # slash command definitions (if any)
│
├── projects/                              # per-project session state + memory
├── plans/                                 # active + archived plans
├── reports/                               # token-usage.md (append-only)
├── backups/                               # precompact-* snapshots + memory-YYYYWW.zip weekly
├── file-history/                          # UUID-keyed file version diffs
├── shell-snapshots/                       # shell context snapshots
├── sessions/                              # session state (ephemeral)
├── session-env/                           # SessionStart artifacts (memory-lint.txt, compact-warning.txt)
├── paste-cache/                           # clipboard cache (ephemeral)
├── downloads/                             # downloaded artifacts
├── telemetry/                             # telemetry queue
├── cache/                                 # generic cache
├── .docs-cache/                           # SHA256 hashes of upstream docs + prefix-version.txt
├── .drift-queue/                          # PostToolUse enqueue → drift-detect-worker drain
│
├── history.jsonl                          # session history log
└── cleanup.log                            # SessionEnd audit trail

%USERPROFILE%\.claude-archive\             [out-of-band backups, separate from live config]
└── rollback-pre-consolidation.zip         # one-shot pre-D-removal snapshot
```

**Anti-pattern**: do not create NTFS junctions to redirect any subdirectory to another volume. The previous D-split design was reverted because it complicated backup tooling, broke drive-letter assumptions in third-party scripts, and provided no measurable benefit at this data scale.

---

## 3. Path Resolution Convention

Every script and document references the config root via:

```powershell
$ClaudeRoot = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) {
    $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
} else {
    Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude'
}
```

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is **not set** in any registry scope — the env var fallback exists only to honor user overrides if a future need arises. The default code path always resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.

In documentation: use `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows-native, expands in cmd / PowerShell / Git Bash) or `~/.claude/` for compactness.

**Forbidden**: relocating the `.claude` config root to a non-profile drive (`D:\.claude\`, `D:\.claude-data\`). D-drive paths in project content are fine — the rule targets the infra root, not the project.

---

## 4. Hook Architecture

Seven hook events are registered in `settings.json` (plus a `statusLine` renderer). SessionEnd registers two command entries, so total command count is eight. See `AUTOMATION.md` for the full sequence diagram and the auto-generated registration table.

| Event | Purpose | Async |
|---|---|---|
| SessionStart | regenerate AUTO-marks, auto-pin, memory-lint, weekly memory-backup, 24h doc gate, 60d plan archive, **D-remnant detection → oneshot consolidation** | no |
| SessionEnd | retention rotations (13 categories), MEMORY.md link integrity, kill stale workers, drift queue drain | yes |
| PostToolUse (Edit\|Write\|Bash) | enqueue edited files / dep-install audits to `.drift-queue` | yes |
| UserPromptSubmit | inject git status + recent commits when repo is dirty (skip-when-clean keeps prompt cache warm) | no |
| PreCompact | hard-link snapshot of MUST-preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>` | no |
| PostCompact | verify `@import` chains + active plan readability; write `compact-warning.txt` on issues | yes |
| Stop | append rtk session stats to `reports/token-usage.md` | yes |
| statusLine | render status line (includes `compact:warn` indicator if PostCompact flagged a loss) | (poll) |

**Design principle**: each hook runs in <100 ms in the synchronous path. Heavier work (`check-updates-worker`) is spawned detached via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`. Detached workers survive parent exit; PowerShell jobs do not.

---

## 5. Retention Policy

Configured in `cleanup.ps1`. Pinned projects (via `active-projects.json`) are exempt from `projects/` rotation.

| Directory | Retention | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `plans/` | 2 days (file mtime) | drafts; archived plans go to `plans/archive/` after 60d |
| `shell-snapshots/` | 7 days | session shell context |
| `file-history/` | 14 days (dir mtime) | UUID-keyed |
| `projects/` | 30 days (dir mtime) | pinned + 14d grace exempt |
| `session-env/` | empty subdirs only | per-session SessionStart outputs |
| `backups/precompact-*` | 28 days | pre-compaction snapshots |
| `backups/memory-*.zip` | 56 days | weekly memory archive |
| `.docs-cache/` | 90 days (file mtime) | SHA hashes regenerable |
| `.drift-queue/` | 7 days | post-drain leftovers |
| `cache/` | 14 days | generic |
| `downloads/` | 30 days | |
| `paste-cache/` | 7 days | clipboard |
| `telemetry/` | 30 days | |

Stale background workers >24h old are killed by command-line pattern match against `<ClaudeRoot>\hooks\`.

---

## 6. Compaction Policy (REWIND CONTEXT)

When Claude Code reaches its context budget and triggers compaction:

**MUST preserve** (load-bearing): active plan, all rule files (`CLAUDE.md` / `RTK.md` / `AUTOMATION.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md`), `settings.json`, per-project active `MEMORY.md`, memory topic files modified within last 30 days.

**MAY drop** (regenerable): plans older than 60 days, `.docs-cache/*`, `cleanup.log`, completed prior-turn todos, intermediate exploration output.

**Hooks**: `precompact-snapshot.ps1` hard-links the preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>/`. `postcompact-verify.ps1` validates `@import` chains and active-plan readability — writes `session-env/compact-warning.txt` on failure, which `statusline.ps1` surfaces as `compact:warn`.

**Anti-pattern**: snapshotting `sessions/` or `file-history/` "just in case" — unbounded growth with no recovery use case (FOMO trap).

---

## 7. RTK Strategy (Token Optimization)

RTK is a Rust-based CLI output filter (60–90% token savings). On this machine:

- **Mode**: explicit prefix only (`rtk <command>`). Hook-based auto-rewrite is a WSL-only feature and is not used here.
- **Coverage**: noisy multi-line outputs (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files, `gh pr`, package managers).
- **Skip**: single-line outputs (`echo`, `pwd`).

Detailed savings table: see `RTK.md`.

---

## 8. Order Match Verification

Every non-trivial task ends with a self-verification step before the AI declares completion. Procedure (full template at `templates/order-match-checklist.md`):

1. Restate the user's order verbatim.
2. List acceptance criteria (observable state).
3. Map each criterion to evidence (`file:line`, command output, test result).
4. Detect scope creep — anything done outside the order? Justify or revert.
5. Honor constraints — language (Korean chat / English AI artifacts), paths (no `D:\.claude`), tools, banned actions.

If any criterion lacks evidence: do **not** declare done. Either complete the gap or report it explicitly.

This rule is the system's primary safeguard against the "AI says done but didn't actually finish" failure mode.

---

## 9. Vanilla Compliance + FOMO Guard

Two principles that govern every change to this setup:

### Vanilla compliance

The closer to stock Claude Code behavior, the easier upgrades and debugging become. Do **not** customize unless an incident or measurable cost forced it. Document the trigger when adding any non-default rule.

Current non-vanilla customizations and their justifications:

| Customization | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` | productivity in trusted host environment |
| 7 hook events (8 command entries — SessionEnd registers 2) in `settings.json` | upstream doc drift, plan rotation, prompt cache invalidation |
| `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` env | 1h prompt cache TTL for token efficiency |
| `effortLevel = "high"` | model output quality preference |
| 13-category retention in `cleanup.ps1` | unbounded growth in volatile dirs |

### FOMO guard

A feature looking interesting is not justification. Before adding a hook / script / rule / skill / plugin, point to:

- a past incident the change prevents, OR
- a measurable benefit (token savings, time savings, error reduction)

If neither exists: skip it.

---

## 10. AI Tool Exclusivity

Claude Code is the sole AI assistant on this machine.

- **Removed**: Codex CLI (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex`), Cursor (`%APPDATA%\Cursor`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-updater`).
- **Pending uninstall** (out of architecture scope, user-driven): VS Code extensions `openai.chatgpt-*`, `github.copilot-chat-*`, Cursor app binaries.

Rationale: split AI surfaces produce conflicting context, duplicate token costs, and inconsistent rule application. One assistant = one rule set = predictable behavior.

---

## 11. Language Convention

| Audience | Language |
|---|---|
| User-facing chat replies | Korean |
| AI-consumed artifacts (docs, hooks, plans, memory, comments, log lines) | **English** |
| Code identifiers, paths, commands, error messages | English (verbatim, regardless of context) |
| Quoted user phrases (e.g. "완료" / "done") | preserved as-is in either language |

Rationale: AI consumption efficiency. English keeps tokens predictable across models and avoids encoding ambiguity (PowerShell 5.1 ANSI codepage corrupts em-dash and similar non-ASCII glyphs).

---

## 12. Migration History

| Date | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-28 | D-drive split (config on C, data on D via NTFS junctions) | initial separation experiment |
| 2026-04-28 | **Reverted to C-only single-drive** | cognitive complexity > benefit at 165 MB scale |
| 2026-04-28 | Codex / Cursor configs removed (12.1 GB reclaimed) | AI tool exclusivity |
| 2026-04-28 | `cleanup.ps1` extended (7 → 13 retention categories) | unbounded growth gap |
| 2026-04-28 | DO / DON'T format adopted in `CLAUDE.md` / `RTK.md` | rule clarity |
| 2026-04-28 | Order Match Verification introduced | "AI says done but didn't" failure mode |
| 2026-04-28 | Compaction policy formalized | REWIND CONTEXT optimization |
| 2026-04-28 | `permissions.deny` redesigned (8 → 24 portable patterns) | Old rules used `%USERPROFILE%` (cmd-only literal, doesn't expand in Bash) and hardcoded the username, so real destructive inputs (`~/.claude`, `/c/Users/...`, `C:/Users/...`) bypassed every rule. New set covers all shell forms and is account-agnostic. Colon-form `:*` aligned to space/inline form per official permission spec. Added `git clean`, `git checkout -- *`, `git restore .`, `**/.env*`. |
| 2026-04-28 | Project `.claude/settings.json` deny added (Drive policy enforcement) | Project AGENTS.md (per-project, not a global file) declared "D: drive only for project work" but no rule enforced it. Project-level deny overrides user-level (precedence: Project > User), so this is the layer that actually blocks `Write/Edit/rm -rf` on `C:\` from project context. Global infra edits now require `update-config` skill or an explicit `~/.claude` session. |

---

## 13. Maintenance Checklist

Run periodically (weekly recommended):

- [ ] `cleanup.log` — recent SessionEnd audit lines show all 13 retention counters firing.
- [ ] `docs-updates.md` — review any new entries from `check-updates-worker.ps1`.
- [ ] `review-needed.md` — drain drift findings.
- [ ] `reports/token-usage.md` — confirm rtk savings ratio is healthy (>50% on heavy days).
- [ ] `Get-PSDrive C` — free space stable; no runaway growth in `projects/` / `file-history/`.
- [ ] `Test-Path D:\.claude*` — must return `False` (single-drive guarantee).
- [ ] Architecture deltas not yet documented here? Append to section 12.

68	| Auto-apply | Never | Docs are prose; translating to rule changes requires human judgment. Silent drift is worse than no automation |
69	| Hash algorithm | SHA256 | Detects any content change; immune to CDN `Last-Modified` header inconsistencies |
70	| ETag vs hash | Hash | `Invoke-WebRequest` in PowerShell 5.1 does not expose ETag cleanly; SHA256 is explicit and portable |

# Claude Code Session Automation

_Architecture document. Static sections: architect-maintained. Marked sections between `<!-- AUTO:* -->` tags are regenerated by `hooks/update-docs.ps1` on every SessionStart — do not edit those sections by hand._

**Last verified**: 2026-04-28T13:59:47+09:00 <!-- AUTO:TIMESTAMP -->

---

## Why this exists

Claude Code loads `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\CLAUDE.md`, rule files, and related configs at every session start. If Anthropic updates official guidance (CLAUDE.md size limits, hook API shape, settings schema, best practices), those local rules silently become stale. Manual checking is unreliable at scale.

This automation closes that gap with three responsibilities:

1. **Upstream detection** — SHA256-based diff of 5 key official docs + GitHub Releases API for the CLI itself. No user action required.
2. **Non-intrusive notification** — changes accumulate in `docs-updates.md`. No popups, no blocking, no auto-edits.
3. **Plan hygiene** — plan files older than 60 days are archived so `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\plans\` stays navigable.

---

## Data flow

```
Claude Code SessionStart
         |
         v
 session-start.ps1  ──── calls (sequentially) ────────────────────────────────┐
         |                                                                      |
         |──► update-docs.ps1         regenerate AUTOMATION.md marked sections |
         |──► archive-plans.ps1       move 60d+ plan files to plans/archive/   |
         v──► check-updates.ps1       24h gate check                           |
                   |                                                            |
              passed 24h?                                                       |
              no ──► exit (noop)                                               |
              yes                                                               |
                   |                                                            |
                   v                                                            |
         Start-Process detached ──► check-updates-worker.ps1                  |
                                              |                                |
                              ┌───────────────┴──────────────────┐            |
                              v                                   v            |
                    GitHub Releases API             5x docs SHA256 diff        |
                    /anthropics/claude-code         memory / hooks /           |
                    /releases/latest                best-practices /           |
                              |                     settings /                 |
                              └───────────────┬─────context-window             |
                                              v                                |
                                      any change?                              |
                                      no ──► exit silently                    |
                                      yes                                      |
                                              v                                |
                                 %USERPROFILE%\.claude\docs-updates.md                   |
                                 (append entry, user reads at leisure)         |
                                                                               |
session starts normally — zero blocking latency ◄──────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Design decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger mechanism | `SessionStart` hook in `settings.json` | Anthropic's documented API — survives Claude Code upgrades without custom tooling |
| Session start latency | `async: true` + detached worker | `session-start.ps1` completes in <100ms; network work happens detached after session opens |
| Worker isolation | `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden` | Detached process survives when PowerShell parent exits; jobs do not |
| Network failures | `try/catch` + `SilentlyContinue` | Network errors must never block a dev session |
| Auto-apply | Never | Docs are prose; translating to rule changes requires human judgment. Silent drift is worse than no automation |
| Hash algorithm | SHA256 | Detects any content change; immune to CDN `Last-Modified` header inconsistencies |
| ETag vs hash | Hash | `Invoke-WebRequest` in PowerShell 5.1 does not expose ETag cleanly; SHA256 is explicit and portable |
| First-run behavior | Silent baseline | Establishes cache without generating noise; notification only fires on next change |
| Rate limit guard | 24h timestamp file | GitHub API: 60 req/h unauthenticated; `last-check.txt` prevents hammering across rapid restarts |
| Archive threshold | 60 days | Long enough that active WIP plans survive; short enough to prevent indefinite accumulation |
| Doc update strategy | Marker-based in-place replacement | Preserves static architect commentary while keeping generated data current |
| PowerShell encoding | ASCII-safe separators (`->`) | PowerShell 5.1 defaults to ANSI codepage; em-dash (U+2014) gets corrupted — explicit ASCII prevents this |

---

## Compaction Policy (REWIND CONTEXT)

When Claude Code reaches its context budget and triggers compaction, the goal is to **preserve the smallest set of artifacts that lets the next turn continue coherently**. The PreCompact and PostCompact hooks enforce this.

### MUST preserve (load-bearing)

- Active plan file under `plans/` (most recent mtime)
- All rule files: `CLAUDE.md`, `RTK.md`, `AUTOMATION.md`, project `.claude/rules/`
- `settings.json`
- Per-project `MEMORY.md` index for active project (resolved via `active-projects.json`)
- Memory topic files (`projects/<name>/memory/*.md`) modified in last 30 days

### MAY drop (regenerable or stale)

- Plans older than 60 days (already archived by `archive-plans.ps1`)
- `.docs-cache/*` — regenerable from upstream on next 24h gate
- `cleanup.log` — append-only audit, not load-bearing
- Completed todo lists from prior turns
- Intermediate exploration output (file reads, grep results) — re-fetchable

### Hook responsibilities

- `precompact-snapshot.ps1`: hard-link the MUST-preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>/` so a postmortem can recover anything dropped accidentally.
- `postcompact-verify.ps1`: confirm `@import` chains in `CLAUDE.md`/`RTK.md` still resolve and the active plan file is still readable. Surface broken refs via stderr — Claude reacts in the next turn.
- `statusline.ps1`: shows `compact:warn` if the most recent post-compact verification flagged a loss.

### Anti-pattern

Manually editing `precompact-snapshot.ps1` to also snapshot `projects/<name>/sessions/` or `file-history/` is a **FOMO trap** — the snapshot grows unboundedly with no recovery use case. Stay with the MUST-preserve set above unless an incident proves otherwise.

---

## Files

<!-- AUTO:SCRIPTS-START -->
| Script | Description | Modified |
|---|---|---|
| `archive-plans.ps1` | Archive plan files older than 60 days into ~/.claude/plans/archive/. | 2026-04-28 |
| `auto-pin.ps1` | Auto-register current project into active-projects.json pinned list on SessionStart. | 2026-04-28 |
| `check-updates.ps1` | SessionStart trigger: 24h gate, then spawn worker detached. | 2026-04-28 |
| `check-updates-worker.ps1` | Detached worker: SHA-diff Claude Code release + key official docs; append findings to docs-updates.md and queue impact sections to review-needed.md. | 2026-04-28 |
| `drift-detect-worker.ps1` | Drift detector worker: drain .drift-queue, append findings to ~/.claude/review-needed.md. | 2026-04-28 |
| `drift-enqueue.ps1` | PostToolUse hook: enqueue edited file paths and dep-install commands. | 2026-04-28 |
| `inject-runtime-ctx.ps1` | UserPromptSubmit hook: inject git runtime context only when the repo is dirty. | 2026-04-28 |
| `memory-backup.ps1` | Weekly snapshot of every project memory dir into ~/.claude/backups/memory-YYYYWW.zip. | 2026-04-28 |
| `memory-lint.ps1` | Lightweight memory integrity check on SessionStart. | 2026-04-28 |
| `oneshot-consolidate.ps1` | One-shot D-drive consolidation worker. | 2026-04-28 |
| `postcompact-verify.ps1` | PostCompact hook: verify @import chain integrity in core AI-consumed files | 2026-04-28 |
| `precompact-snapshot.ps1` | PreCompact hook: snapshot project memory + active plans via hard-links. | 2026-04-28 |
| `session-start.ps1` | SessionStart entry point. Calls all session-start tasks in order. | 2026-04-28 |
| `token-report.ps1` | Stop hook: append rtk session stats to ~/.claude/reports/token-usage.md. | 2026-04-28 |
| `update-docs.ps1` | Regenerate AUTO-marked sections in ~/.claude/AUTOMATION.md on every session start. | 2026-04-28 |
<!-- AUTO:SCRIPTS-END -->

---

## Hook events

_Sourced from `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json`. Auto-regenerated on SessionStart by `update-docs.ps1`._

<!-- AUTO:HOOK-EVENTS-START -->
| Event | Matcher | Async | Command (truncated) |
|---|---|---|---|
| PostCompact | * | yes | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/postcompact...` |
| PostToolUse | Edit|Write|Bash | yes | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/drift-enque...` |
| PreCompact | * | no | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/precompact-...` |
| SessionEnd | * | yes | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/cleanup.ps1"` |
| SessionEnd | * | yes | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/drift-detec...` |
| SessionStart | * | no | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/session-sta...` |
| Stop | * | yes | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/token-repor...` |
| UserPromptSubmit | * | no | `powershell.exe -NonInteractive -File "%USERPROFILE%/.claude/hooks/inject-runt...` |
<!-- AUTO:HOOK-EVENTS-END -->

---

## Skills

_Sourced from `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\<name>\SKILL.md` frontmatter (`name` + `description`)._

<!-- AUTO:SKILLS-START -->
| Skill | Description |
|---|---|
| _(none registered)_ |  |
<!-- AUTO:SKILLS-END -->

---

## Monitored sources

| Source | Cache key | What it detects |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code release | `release-tag.txt` | New CLI versions (bug fixes, new hook events, settings changes) |
| `memory.md` | `memory.sha256` | CLAUDE.md best practices, size limits (currently 200 lines) |
| `hooks.md` | `hooks.sha256` | Hook event types, payload schema, timeout behavior |
| `best-practices.md` | `best-practices.sha256` | General guidance, anti-patterns |
| `settings.md` | `settings.sha256` | `settings.json` supported keys and defaults |
| `context-window.md` | `context-window.sha256` | Startup context budget breakdown (affects rule file sizing) |

---

## Cache layout

```
%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.docs-cache\
├── last-check.txt          # ISO8601 timestamp of last trigger run (24h gate)
├── release-tag.txt         # Last seen Claude Code release tag (e.g. v2.1.119)
├── memory.sha256           # SHA256 of last fetched memory.md
├── hooks.sha256
├── best-practices.sha256
├── settings.sha256
└── context-window.sha256
```

---

## Output format

`%USERPROFILE%\.claude\docs-updates.md` is append-only. Each session that detects changes appends a dated block:

```markdown
## 2026-04-27
- **Claude Code release**: v2.1.120 (was: v2.1.119) -> https://github.com/...
- **Doc updated**: memory -> https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md
```

The user reviews this file and decides whether to update `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or global rules. Nothing is auto-applied.

---

## Extending

### Add a new monitored doc page

1. Open `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\hooks\check-updates-worker.ps1`
2. Add an entry to the `$docs` array:
   ```powershell
   @{ name = 'your-page'; url = 'https://code.claude.com/docs/en/your-page.md' }
   ```
3. Done — next session start populates the baseline hash silently; subsequent changes trigger notification.

### Add a new session-start task

1. Create `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\hooks\your-task.ps1`. First line **must** be a `# Short description` comment — this feeds `update-docs.ps1`.
2. Add `& "$PSScriptRoot\your-task.ps1"` to `session-start.ps1`.
3. `update-docs.ps1` auto-discovers all `*.ps1` in `hooks/` on next session and updates this document.

### Force a refresh (bypass 24h gate)

```powershell
Remove-Item %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.docs-cache\last-check.txt
# Then restart Claude Code or run session-start.ps1 manually
```

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `docs-updates.md` never created | Worker failing silently | Run `check-updates-worker.ps1` in an interactive PowerShell to see errors |
| Only `release-tag.txt` in cache, no `.sha256` files | Stale worker before the `byte[]` fix | Delete cache dir and run worker again |
| Release tag not updating | GitHub API rate limit (60/h) | Check `last-check.txt` timestamp — if <24h ago, wait |
| `AUTOMATION.md` markers not updating | `update-docs.ps1` not called | Verify `session-start.ps1` includes the call |
| Plan files not archived | All files < 60 days old | Expected — archive only triggers after 60 days of inactivity |
| Korean text garbled in docs | PowerShell ANSI codepage | All scripts use `-Encoding UTF8`; ensure editor reads as UTF-8 |

---

## Related files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json` | Registers `SessionStart` hook pointing to `session-start.ps1` |
| `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\docs-updates.md` | Auto-created on first detected change; append-only notification log |
| `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.docs-cache\` | Hash/tag/timestamp cache; safe to delete for forced refresh |
| `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\plans\archive\` | Destination for 60d+ archived plan files |

1	# Claude Code Harness Architecture (Anthropic-Native Pattern)
2	
3	This document defines the **architecture pattern** used to organize rules, hooks, memory, and skills across every project on this machine. It is project-agnostic — any new project should read this before adding harness configuration.
4	
5	Companion docs:
6	- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — this-machine operations (directory layout, retention, hooks installed)
7	- `CLAUDE.md` — global operating rules (DO / DON'T)
8	- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
9	- `AUTOMATION.md` — auto-generated hook registration table
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Why This Pattern (Decision Record)
14	
15	We evaluated three candidate architectures for the harness layer:
16	
17	| Candidate | Verdict | Evidence |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| Domain-Driven Design (bounded contexts, aggregates, anti-corruption layer) | **Rejected** | Zero official agent framework recommends DDD for harness. OpenAI Swarm, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, CrewAI, Anthropic — all silent or use opposite (flat) patterns. Community Medium/ODSC posts mention DDD aspirationally; no official doc adopts it. |
20	| SOLID as primary architecture | **Partial only** | Applies to hook/skill *code*, not to JSON/Markdown configuration. Settings precedence (Managed → Project → User → Local) and deny-list accumulation are policy-precedence, not polymorphic substitution. |
21	| **Anthropic-native** (Progressive Disclosure + Hook Event Model + Plan-Verify Loop) | **Adopted** | Officially documented and named by Anthropic. Aligns with cross-vendor patterns (Microsoft 5-orchestration types, LangGraph stateful graph, CrewAI YAML manifest, Swarm stateless handoff) at the points where they converge. |
22	
23	**Sources** (authoritative only):
24	- https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents
25	- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks
26	- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory
27	- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/best-practices
28	- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills
29	- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/settings
30	- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents
31	
32	This decision is final. If a future project tries to reintroduce DDD framing, point at this section.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 2. The Pattern (3 Layers + Verification Loop)
37	
38	```
39	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
40	│  LAYER 1 — ALWAYS-LOADED CONTEXT                                │
41	│                                                                 │
42	│  CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md   ≤200 lines combined target             │
43	│  MEMORY.md (auto-memory) index, ≤25 KB                          │
44	│                                                                 │
45	│  Rule: only what EVERY session needs                            │
46	└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
47	                           │
48	┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
49	│  LAYER 2 — PATH-SCOPED / ON-DEMAND                              │
50	│                                                                 │
51	│  .claude/rules/<topic>.md      loaded when files match `paths:` │
52	│  memory/<topic>.md             loaded by MEMORY.md link click   │
53	│  .claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md   invoked, never auto-loaded   │
54	│  .claude/agents/<agent>.md     invoked via Agent tool           │
55	│                                                                 │
56	│  Rule: domain-specific knowledge that costs context             │
57	└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
58	                           │
59	┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
60	│  LAYER 3 — HOOK-ENFORCED DETERMINISM                            │
61	│                                                                 │
62	│  PreToolUse[Bash]  rewrite tool input   (e.g. rtk-prerewrite)   │
63	│  PostToolUse       file-type checks     (tsc / vitest / lint)   │
64	│  PreCompact/Post   memory snapshot integrity                    │
65	│  SessionStart/End  retention + drift drain                      │
66	│  Stop              token-report append                          │
67	│  permissions.deny  structural blocks (rm -rf, force push, etc.) │
68	│                                                                 │
69	│  Rule: any policy that must hold "zero exceptions"              │
70	└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
71	                           │ executes
72	                  [ COMMAND EXECUTION ]
73	                           │
74	┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
75	│  VERIFICATION LOOP                                              │
76	│                                                                 │
77	│  rtk gain          quantitative coverage (was RTK applied?)     │
78	│  rtk discover      qualitative gaps (which commands missed?)    │
79	│  .drift-queue/     edit drift signals                           │
80	│  reports/*.md      append-only audit trail                      │
81	│                                                                 │
82	│  Feedback rule: if gap detected, fix Layer 3, NOT Layer 1 docs  │
83	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
84	```
85	
86	**Anthropic naming** (use these terms, not "domain"/"aggregate"):
87	- "Progressive Disclosure" — the layered loading mechanism for skills
88	- "Hook Event Model" — Layer 3
89	- "Plan-Verify Loop" / "Verification" — the loop above
90	- "Augmented LLM" / "Orchestrator-Workers" — when planning multi-agent flows
91	- "Precedence Hierarchy" — settings cascade (Managed > Project > User > Local)
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 3. What Goes Where (Decision Matrix)
96	
97	When adding ANY new piece of configuration, ask:
98	
99	| Question | If yes → place in | Example |
100	|---|---|---|
101	| Does every session need this loaded into context? | Layer 1 (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) | "Reply in Korean", "Don't run npm build" |
102	| Does it apply only to specific file types or paths? | Layer 2 (`.claude/rules/<topic>.md` with `paths:` frontmatter) | TypeScript-only rules, SCSS-only rules |
103	| Is it persistent learning across sessions for this project? | Layer 2 (`memory/<topic>.md` linked from MEMORY.md) | "User prefers terse responses", project architecture map |
104	| Is it a multi-step procedure that the user invokes? | Layer 2 (`.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`) | `/new-route`, `/audit-harness` |
105	| Must it hold every time, no exceptions, even mid-task? | Layer 3 (hook in `settings.json`) | RTK auto-prefix, file-type lint |
106	| Is it a structural prohibition (data destruction, credential exfil)? | Layer 3 (`permissions.deny`) | `rm -rf`, force push, `.credentials*` reads |
107	
108	**If you can't answer — don't add it.** That's the FOMO gate (see §5).
109	
110	---
111	
112	## 4. Extension Recipes
113	
114	### 4.1 Add a Layer 1 rule (advisory, every session)
115	
116	1. Open project `AGENTS.md` (cross-AI) or `CLAUDE.md` (Claude-specific delta).
117	2. Add the rule under the correct heading. Keep wording terse.
118	3. **Verify**: `rtk grep -c "" CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md` — combined ≤200 lines.
119	4. If combined exceeds 200 lines: move the least-frequently-needed rule to Layer 2.
120	
121	### 4.2 Add a Layer 2 path-scoped rule
122	
123	1. Create `.claude/rules/<topic>.md` with frontmatter:
124	   ```markdown
125	   ---
126	   paths: ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx"]
127	   ---
128	   ```
129	2. The rule loads only when Claude touches files matching `paths:`.
130	3. Keep each `<topic>.md` focused — one concern per file.
131	4. **Verify**: open a file matching the glob, confirm Claude references the rule.
132	
133	### 4.3 Add a Layer 2 memory topic (project learning)
134	
135	1. Create `memory/<topic>.md` under the project's auto-memory dir (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`).
136	2. Frontmatter: `name`, `description`, `type` (user / feedback / project / reference).
137	3. Add one line to `MEMORY.md` index: `- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook`.
138	4. **Verify**: `MEMORY.md` index stays ≤200 lines / ≤25 KB. Description on the index line should match the topic file's frontmatter `name`.
139	
140	### 4.4 Add a Layer 2 skill (invoked procedure)
141	
142	1. Create `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name`, `description`.
143	2. Body is the procedure — multi-step, cross-cutting. Static facts belong in rules, not skills.
144	3. **FOMO gate**: skill must plausibly run ≥3× per month, otherwise inline the steps in a rule.
145	4. **Verify**: invoke via `/<skill>` from Claude Code; confirm SKILL.md content enters the conversation as a single message (Anthropic Progressive Disclosure level 2).
146	
147	### 4.5 Add a Layer 3 hook
148	
149	1. Implement the handler in `~/.claude/hooks/<name>.{js,ps1}`.
150	2. Schema: read JSON from stdin, optionally write JSON to stdout (`{"modified_input":{...}}` to rewrite, empty to pass through, exit code `2` to block).
151	3. Register in `~/.claude/settings.json` under the appropriate event (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Stop`).
152	4. **FOMO gate**: hook must enforce a policy that has FAILED before. Never add a hook because "it would be cool".
153	5. **Verify**: pipe a sample event JSON to the handler manually; confirm output. Then update `AUTOMATION.md` registration table.
154	
155	### 4.6 Add a Layer 3 deny rule
156	
157	1. Append a pattern to `permissions.deny` in `~/.claude/settings.json` (global) or project `.claude/settings.json` (project-only).
158	2. Patterns must be portable across shells — see migration entry 2026-04-28 in ARCHITECTURE.md §12. Cover all path forms: `~/...`, `/c/Users/...`, `C:/Users/...`, `%USERPROFILE%/...`.
159	3. **Verify**: in a sandbox, attempt the denied action — confirm Claude Code refuses it without bypass prompt.
160	
161	### 4.7 Add a verification loop entry
162	
163	1. Identify the metric (e.g., "% of Bash calls that hit the hook").
164	2. Add the check to `hooks/token-report.ps1` (Stop hook) or `hooks/cleanup.ps1` (SessionEnd).
165	3. Append findings to `reports/<metric>.md` (append-only).
166	4. **Anti-pattern**: do NOT make verification block on failure — it must be observable, not enforcing. Enforcement belongs in Layer 3.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 5. Anti-Patterns (Anthropic-explicit warnings)
171	
172	| Anti-pattern | Source | What it looks like here |
173	|---|---|---|

# Claude Code Harness Architecture (Anthropic-Native Pattern)

This document defines the **architecture pattern** used to organize rules, hooks, memory, and skills across every project on this machine. It is project-agnostic — any new project should read this before adding harness configuration.

Companion docs:
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — this-machine operations (directory layout, retention, hooks installed)
- `CLAUDE.md` — global operating rules (DO / DON'T)
- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
- `AUTOMATION.md` — auto-generated hook registration table

---

## 1. Why This Pattern (Decision Record)

We evaluated three candidate architectures for the harness layer:

| Candidate | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Domain-Driven Design (bounded contexts, aggregates, anti-corruption layer) | **Rejected** | Zero official agent framework recommends DDD for harness. OpenAI Swarm, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, CrewAI, Anthropic — all silent or use opposite (flat) patterns. Community Medium/ODSC posts mention DDD aspirationally; no official doc adopts it. |
| SOLID as primary architecture | **Partial only** | Applies to hook/skill *code*, not to JSON/Markdown configuration. Settings precedence (Managed → Project → User → Local) and deny-list accumulation are policy-precedence, not polymorphic substitution. |
| **Anthropic-native** (Progressive Disclosure + Hook Event Model + Plan-Verify Loop) | **Adopted** | Officially documented and named by Anthropic. Aligns with cross-vendor patterns (Microsoft 5-orchestration types, LangGraph stateful graph, CrewAI YAML manifest, Swarm stateless handoff) at the points where they converge. |

**Sources** (authoritative only):
- https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents
- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks
- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory
- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/best-practices
- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills
- https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/settings
- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents

This decision is final. If a future project tries to reintroduce DDD framing, point at this section.

---

## 2. The Pattern (3 Layers + Verification Loop)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 1 — ALWAYS-LOADED CONTEXT                                │
│                                                                 │
│  CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md   ≤200 lines combined target             │
│  MEMORY.md (auto-memory) index, ≤25 KB                          │
│                                                                 │
│  Rule: only what EVERY session needs                            │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 2 — PATH-SCOPED / ON-DEMAND                              │
│                                                                 │
│  .claude/rules/<topic>.md      loaded when files match `paths:` │
│  memory/<topic>.md             loaded by MEMORY.md link click   │
│  .claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md   invoked, never auto-loaded   │
│  .claude/agents/<agent>.md     invoked via Agent tool           │
│                                                                 │
│  Rule: domain-specific knowledge that costs context             │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 3 — HOOK-ENFORCED DETERMINISM                            │
│                                                                 │
│  PreToolUse[Bash]  rewrite tool input   (e.g. rtk-prerewrite)   │
│  PostToolUse       file-type checks     (tsc / vitest / lint)   │
│  PreCompact/Post   memory snapshot integrity                    │
│  SessionStart/End  retention + drift drain                      │
│  Stop              token-report append                          │
│  permissions.deny  structural blocks (rm -rf, force push, etc.) │
│                                                                 │
│  Rule: any policy that must hold "zero exceptions"              │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ executes
                  [ COMMAND EXECUTION ]
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  VERIFICATION LOOP                                              │
│                                                                 │
│  rtk gain          quantitative coverage (was RTK applied?)     │
│  rtk discover      qualitative gaps (which commands missed?)    │
│  .drift-queue/     edit drift signals                           │
│  reports/*.md      append-only audit trail                      │
│                                                                 │
│  Feedback rule: if gap detected, fix Layer 3, NOT Layer 1 docs  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Anthropic naming** (use these terms, not "domain"/"aggregate"):
- "Progressive Disclosure" — the layered loading mechanism for skills
- "Hook Event Model" — Layer 3
- "Plan-Verify Loop" / "Verification" — the loop above
- "Augmented LLM" / "Orchestrator-Workers" — when planning multi-agent flows
- "Precedence Hierarchy" — settings cascade (Managed > Project > User > Local)

---

## 3. What Goes Where (Decision Matrix)

When adding ANY new piece of configuration, ask:

| Question | If yes → place in | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Does every session need this loaded into context? | Layer 1 (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) | "Reply in Korean", "Don't run npm build" |
| Does it apply only to specific file types or paths? | Layer 2 (`.claude/rules/<topic>.md` with `paths:` frontmatter) | TypeScript-only rules, SCSS-only rules |
| Is it persistent learning across sessions for this project? | Layer 2 (`memory/<topic>.md` linked from MEMORY.md) | "User prefers terse responses", project architecture map |
| Is it a multi-step procedure that the user invokes? | Layer 2 (`.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`) | `/new-route`, `/audit-harness` |
| Must it hold every time, no exceptions, even mid-task? | Layer 3 (hook in `settings.json`) | RTK auto-prefix, file-type lint |
| Is it a structural prohibition (data destruction, credential exfil)? | Layer 3 (`permissions.deny`) | `rm -rf`, force push, `.credentials*` reads |

**If you can't answer — don't add it.** That's the FOMO gate (see §5).

---

## 4. Extension Recipes

### 4.1 Add a Layer 1 rule (advisory, every session)

1. Open project `AGENTS.md` (cross-AI) or `CLAUDE.md` (Claude-specific delta).
2. Add the rule under the correct heading. Keep wording terse.
3. **Verify**: `rtk grep -c "" CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md` — combined ≤200 lines.
4. If combined exceeds 200 lines: move the least-frequently-needed rule to Layer 2.

### 4.2 Add a Layer 2 path-scoped rule

1. Create `.claude/rules/<topic>.md` with frontmatter:
   ```markdown
   ---
   paths: ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx"]
   ---
   ```
2. The rule loads only when Claude touches files matching `paths:`.
3. Keep each `<topic>.md` focused — one concern per file.
4. **Verify**: open a file matching the glob, confirm Claude references the rule.

### 4.3 Add a Layer 2 memory topic (project learning)

1. Create `memory/<topic>.md` under the project's auto-memory dir (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`).
2. Frontmatter: `name`, `description`, `type` (user / feedback / project / reference).
3. Add one line to `MEMORY.md` index: `- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook`.
4. **Verify**: `MEMORY.md` index stays ≤200 lines / ≤25 KB. Description on the index line should match the topic file's frontmatter `name`.

### 4.4 Add a Layer 2 skill (invoked procedure)

1. Create `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name`, `description`.
2. Body is the procedure — multi-step, cross-cutting. Static facts belong in rules, not skills.
3. **FOMO gate**: skill must plausibly run ≥3× per month, otherwise inline the steps in a rule.
4. **Verify**: invoke via `/<skill>` from Claude Code; confirm SKILL.md content enters the conversation as a single message (Anthropic Progressive Disclosure level 2).

### 4.5 Add a Layer 3 hook

1. Implement the handler in `~/.claude/hooks/<name>.{js,ps1}`.
2. Schema: read JSON from stdin, optionally write JSON to stdout (`{"modified_input":{...}}` to rewrite, empty to pass through, exit code `2` to block).
3. Register in `~/.claude/settings.json` under the appropriate event (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Stop`).
4. **FOMO gate**: hook must enforce a policy that has FAILED before. Never add a hook because "it would be cool".
5. **Verify**: pipe a sample event JSON to the handler manually; confirm output. Then update `AUTOMATION.md` registration table.

### 4.6 Add a Layer 3 deny rule

1. Append a pattern to `permissions.deny` in `~/.claude/settings.json` (global) or project `.claude/settings.json` (project-only).
2. Patterns must be portable across shells — see migration entry 2026-04-28 in ARCHITECTURE.md §12. Cover all path forms: `~/...`, `/c/Users/...`, `C:/Users/...`, `%USERPROFILE%/...`.
3. **Verify**: in a sandbox, attempt the denied action — confirm Claude Code refuses it without bypass prompt.

### 4.7 Add a verification loop entry

1. Identify the metric (e.g., "% of Bash calls that hit the hook").
2. Add the check to `hooks/token-report.ps1` (Stop hook) or `hooks/cleanup.ps1` (SessionEnd).
3. Append findings to `reports/<metric>.md` (append-only).
4. **Anti-pattern**: do NOT make verification block on failure — it must be observable, not enforcing. Enforcement belongs in Layer 3.

---

## 5. Anti-Patterns (Anthropic-explicit warnings)

| Anti-pattern | Source | What it looks like here |
|---|---|---|
| Over-specified CLAUDE.md | Best Practices | "If your CLAUDE.md is too long, Claude ignores half of it." Combined CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md must stay ≤200 lines. |
| Kitchen-sink session | Best Practices | Mixing unrelated tasks in one conversation. Use `/clear` between topics. |
| Correcting over and over | Best Practices | After 2 corrections, `/rewind` or `/clear` and rewrite the prompt. |
| One-shot agent | Effective Harnesses | Letting the agent attempt an entire feature in one go. Constrain to one increment per session; commit progress. |
| Hook exit-code confusion | Hooks docs | Many use exit code 1 (non-blocking) when they meant exit code 2 (blocking). Always exit 2 for policy enforcement. |
| FOMO-driven additions | Vanilla compliance | "Skills look interesting" is not a reason. Every new hook/rule/skill must point to a past incident or measurable benefit. |
| Documentation as enforcement | Inferred from Hooks docs | Writing "always do X" in CLAUDE.md instead of installing a hook. If it must hold every time, it goes in Layer 3. |

---

## 6. Cross-Layer Refactoring Cues

When Layer 1 grows beyond budget, push items down:

- Layer 1 entry referenced only when editing TS files → move to `.claude/rules/frontend.md` (Layer 2).
- Layer 1 entry that's actually a procedure (e.g., "before merging, run X then Y then Z") → move to a skill (Layer 2).
- Layer 1 entry that says "always do X for every Bash call" → migrate to a Layer 3 hook and remove from Layer 1.

The MEMORY.md index follows the same discipline: long memories split into topic files; the index keeps one-line pointers.

---

## 7. Per-Project Bootstrap Checklist

For a new project to inherit this architecture:

- [ ] `<project>/AGENTS.md` exists with cross-AI rules (cross-AI superset of Claude-only rules).
- [ ] `<project>/CLAUDE.md` exists with `@AGENTS.md` import on line 1, plus Claude-only deltas.
- [ ] Combined `CLAUDE.md` + `AGENTS.md` ≤ 200 lines.
- [ ] `<project>/.claude/settings.json` exists with project-specific PostToolUse checks (lint/test/typecheck) and project-only deny rules.
- [ ] `<project>/.claude/rules/` contains path-scoped rules with `paths:` frontmatter.
- [ ] `<project>/.claude/skills/` contains only skills used ≥3×/month.
- [ ] `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/MEMORY.md` index exists; topic files referenced are concrete (no dangling links).
- [ ] No documentation contradicts live state (no "feature X is unavailable" while X is installed; no references to files that don't exist).
- [ ] Project does not redefine global Layer 3 hooks — those cascade from `~/.claude/settings.json` automatically.

Template: `~/.claude/templates/project-init.md` (see ARCHITECTURE.md §1 companion list).

---

## 8. When To Update This Document

- A new architectural decision is made (e.g., adopting a new layer, changing the verification loop).
- A new framework or Anthropic doc supersedes the cited sources — update §1 evidence row.
- A new anti-pattern is discovered through incident — append to §5.

Do **not** update for:
- A specific project's rule additions (those live in the project, not here).
- Cosmetic changes to existing layers.
- Migrating a single rule from one layer to another (handled by §6 cues, no doc edit needed).

---

## 9. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Harness | Every piece of code, configuration, and execution logic that isn't the model itself. The thing that turns a raw model into an agent. |
| Layer 1 / 2 / 3 | This document's naming for always-loaded / on-demand / hook-enforced configuration tiers. |
| Progressive Disclosure | Anthropic's term for the layered loading mechanism (originally for Skills, extended here to all harness configuration). |
| Hook Event Model | Anthropic's lifecycle-event system for deterministic enforcement (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, etc.). |
| Plan-Verify Loop | Anthropic Best Practices: Explore → Plan → Implement → Verify → Commit. |
| Precedence Hierarchy | Anthropic settings cascade: Managed > CLI > Local Project > Project > User. |
| Verification Loop | Append-only audit trail (`rtk gain`, `rtk discover`, `.drift-queue`, `reports/*.md`) that detects gaps for Layer 3 fixes. |
| FOMO gate | Decision rule: every new harness item must justify itself with a past incident or measurable benefit, otherwise skip. |

문서를 다 훑어봤습니다. 전체적으로 구조와 원칙(Vanilla compliance / FOMO guard / 3-Layer harness / Order Match)은 잘 잡혀 있는데 **설명과 실제 설정이 어긋난 부분**이 여러 군데 있습니다. 가장 큰 문제부터 정리합니다.

---

## 🔴 치명적: RTK 자동 재작성 훅 — 문서 vs 실제 불일치

`settings.json:38-49`에 `PreToolUse → rtk-prerewrite.js`가 **활성화돼 있습니다**. 그런데 글로벌 문서 4곳이 정반대로 말하고 있습니다.

| 위치 | 잘못된 서술 |
|---|---|
| [CLAUDE.md:8](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L8) | "DON'T propose ... `rtk init -g --auto-patch` hook auto-rewrite. RTK on Windows native is **manual prefix only**" |
| [CLAUDE.md:5](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L5) | "DO prefix Bash commands with `rtk` when output spans more than a few lines (Windows native: explicit prefix only)" |
| [CLAUDE.md:65](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L65) | "RTK on This Machine: Windows native — no auto-rewrite" |
| [RTK.md:13](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/RTK.md#L13) | "This machine is **Windows native**: there is no hook auto-rewrite. Use the explicit prefix." |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md:160](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/ARCHITECTURE.md#L160) | "Mode: explicit prefix only ... Hook-based auto-rewrite is a WSL-only feature and is not used here." |
